name: Burns
source_guidance: Adapted from WHO burns first aid guidance and NHS 111 guidance on burns and scalds. Includes local advice against applying palm oil, toothpaste, or herbs.

questions.text: Is the person unconscious or struggling to breathe, or were they in a fire inside a closed space?
Is there burning around the mouth or nose, a hoarse voice, or soot in the mouth or nose?
Is the burn large, such as a whole arm, leg, chest, or back, or does it go all the way round a limb?
Was it an electrical or chemical burn?
Is the burn on the face, hands, feet, private parts, or over a joint?
Is the skin white, brown, black, or leathery, or are there blisters bigger than the person's palm?
Is the person a child under 5, an older adult over 60, pregnant, or living with diabetes?
Is a small burn not healing after two weeks?

emergency: Call 112 now, or get to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes if it is safe to do so. For chemical burns, rinse with plenty of water.
Remove jewellery and clothing near the burn unless stuck to the skin.
Cover loosely with clean cling film or a clean cloth. Keep the person warm.
Do not apply ice, palm oil, butter, toothpaste, or herbs.
urgent: Go to a hospital or clinic today.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes first.
Cover loosely with clean cling film or a clean cloth.
Do not burst blisters or apply oil, toothpaste, or herbs.
routine: Book a clinic appointment within the next few days.
Keep the burn clean and covered.
Go sooner if the area becomes more red, swollen, smelly, or painful, or if fever starts.
self_care: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Cover loosely with clean cling film or a clean, non-fluffy cloth.
Do not apply ice, palm oil, butter, toothpaste, or herbs. Do not burst blisters.
Paracetamol can be taken as directed on the pack for pain.
Call back if the burn becomes red, swollen, or smelly, or if fever starts.
